completed_stage_receipts.summary: Classified user-facing version namespace ambiguity as a real observability defect; the user's date/SVN suggestion remained a candidate mechanism pending independent assessment.
One understandable revision must be shown without replacing Git SHA, protocol version, controller revision or owner/task state version.
Mapped receipt display, persisted timestamps, monotonic owner/task version, Git identity, protocol compatibility, controller trace, resume behavior, cross-owner adoption and performance.
First-observed namespace-leakage issue; no prior accepted human-revision repair to escalate from.
Studied SVN monotonic revisions, Git tag/describe semantics and CalVer; rejected emulating a centralized global counter across Git repositories.
Reuse authoritative updated_at plus existing monotonic manifest/owner version; no counter service, registry, tag stream or history traversal.
Rejected daily counter, tag-every-commit and SHA-only display; accepted derived <scope>-YYYYMMDD-rN with focused counterexamples.
No user architecture decision required; human revision is derived presentation only.
Existing progress/version authorities own the feature; no account instruction, protocol bump, root policy or ENTRYPOINT expansion.
O(1) derivation from already-loaded metadata; no new remote read, counter, registry or startup preload.
No revision registry and no per-checkpoint Git tags; technical namespaces remain authoritative and the new label is presentation-only.

After the corrective M8 passed, second-order/propagation review found two design-boundary defects in the pilot state: the task manifest carried a stored human_revision_latest_expected copy despite the derived-only rule, and adoption/comparison semantics were underspecified for owner/task-local sequences, skipped internal revisions and owners without a suitable monotonic version. Reopened to M7, removed the stored duplicate, made rN the within-scope ordering signal, allowed gaps, prohibited cross-scope numeric comparison, and added a fail-closed owner adoption gate. Core TaskMetadata/receipt state schemas remain unchanged intentionally; the label is assembled only at the user-facing receipt presentation boundary.

reopen_history.reason: M8 CI 38363727516 / job 115183763873 passed control-plane and architecture checks but full pytest failed 2 tests: controller implementation receipt lacked required prepatch_checkpoint binding, and HANDOFF dropped the protected single-writer/PR-first regression anchor. Reopen to M7 and repair process surfaces without altering the accepted Human Durable Revision design.

Corrective M8 38363967497 / 115184549077 passed, but second-order and cross-owner propagation review found that storing human_revision_latest_expected would create a stale duplicate truth, and that scope-local/gap/adoption semantics needed explicit fail-closed constraints before any future owner rollout. Reopen to M7; keep the core format but remove duplicate storage and harden the display-only boundary.
